qualitative.gate_3m_moat_note: Entitlement hurdles and high land costs in infill coastal gateway markets limit supply; large-scale platform provides minor operational efficiencies across ~184,000 units. However, empirical ROIC is structurally bounded at ~4-6% (well below the 12% hurdle) due to property capital intensity. Primary erosion threats include cyclical apartment supply deliveries, low tenant switching costs on 1-year leases, and municipal rent-control/tenant protection regulations.
qualitative.note: Fails Gate 3b (ROIC = 5.0% < 12%, REJECT). Multi-family residential rental platform lacks empirical proof of moat, with 5-year median GAAP ROIC structurally anchored at ~5% due to property cap rates and capital intensity. Annual lease turnover and tenant substitute shopping prevent pricing power above market clearing rates, compounded by coastal rent-stabilization caps.
qualitative.evidence: Historical median GAAP ROIC of ~5.0% (AvalonBay ~4.8%, Equity Residential ~5.2%), falling far short of the 12.0% hurdle across all business cycles. Portfolio of ~184,000 apartment units concentrated in coastal gateway markets (Boston, NY/NJ, Washington D.C., California, Pacific Northwest). While balance sheet is investment-grade ('A' rated, debt/EBITDA ~5.5x), the underlying real estate asset class cannot achieve the required double-digit ROIC without excessive financial leverage.
